note: Worth County Conservation park west of Northwood, the county's oldest (177 acres of old-growth forest, prairie and glacial potholes). Four primitive electric sites by the playground and open shelter, in a clearing at the head of the lane in from 495th St. No water. Closed in November for gun season. The county calls the sites 'small' and gives no lengths, so whether a 23-ft motorhome fits is unconfirmed. Upland woods; campsites not on water. --Claude
summary: 4 sites, pit toilet / no water, season Apr 15-Oct 31 confirmed from the county's pages; derived reservable:true cleared (no county page offers campsite booking); fees $15 unchanged; amps not stated by the county ('110 service'). Fit unclear ('4 small campsites'): caveat added. Pin ~280 m off in unbroken forest. Note cleaned.
flags: CRITERIA (fit, keep with caveat): the county singles these out as '4 small campsites' with no length given. No review from the last 3 years states the reviewer's own rig length (The Dyrt's 3 reviews and Campendium's 0 say nothing about rig size). Per AWH 2026-11-02 an unclear pad size stays with a caveat; the proposed note carries it.

PIN: stored 43.48411,-93.26716 is in unbroken old-growth canopy ~280 m west of the park's only clearing. Suggest ~43.4838,-93.2637 (the clearing with the open shelter and playground, which the county says is 'across from the campsites'; the four sites themselves aren't distinguishable on imagery). Google's 'Ochee Yahola' sits at the 495th St entrance, 43.48094,-93.26401.

HOOKUPS: the county says '110 electrical service' (volts, no amperage). Two dated camper reviews on The Dyrt (Sep 2026, May 2025) describe the posts as 20 amp; not written, since the county's own page is silent on amps.
